query: Let It Run Lyra lets you into the duel hall after it has closed. She cups her hands and the fire in them grows, and grows, until it lights the rafters. "They taught me to keep it small," she says. "This is what it does when I stop. I've never shown anyone." Ask her to teach you She teaches it the way she does everything, without explaining, twice. Your fire runs on the third try and bites your wrist on the way out. "It does that," she says. "You stop apologising for it eventually." Just watch her let it run You sit on the bench and watch her let it run to the rafters and back. She doesn't offer again tonight. On the way out she says, "Another time," which from Lyra is a promise.
